answer:
**Security Awareness Guidance – Handling Suspicious Documents** Acme India’s security awareness program advises all employees to treat any document that looks unusual, unexpected, or out‑of‑the‑ordinary with caution. The key points are: | Situation | Recommended Action | |-----------|---------------------| | **Unexpected attachment** (e.g., an Excel file from a colleague you haven’t heard from, a PDF from an external vendor you don’t normally deal with) | • Do **not** open the file immediately.
• Verify the sender through a separate channel (e.g., a quick chat or phone call). | | **File name or extension looks odd** (e.g., “Invoice_Final_v2.docx.exe”, “Report.pdf.zip”) | • Do **not** open the file.
• Report it to the IT Security team (security@acme.in). | | **Document requests sensitive data** (e.g., asking for passwords, bank details, personal IDs) | • Treat it as a phishing attempt.
• Forward the document to security@acme.in for analysis. | | **Macro‑enabled Office files** (e.g., *.xlsm, *.docm) that you weren’t expecting | • Disable macros and do not enable them.
• Send the file to security@acme.in before any further action. | | **Links inside the document** that redirect to unknown URLs | • Hover over the link to view the actual URL.
• Do not click unless you have verified the link’s legitimacy. | | **Document appears corrupted or contains garbled text** | • This can be a sign of an embedded malicious payload.
• Delete the file and report it. | ### General Steps to Follow 1. **Do not interact** with the suspicious document until it has been verified. 2. **Verify the sender** through a trusted communication channel (e.g., a phone call, a separate chat message, or an internal directory lookup). 3. **Report** the document to the IT Security team at **security@acme.in**. Include: - The original email (with headers, if possible). - The file name and type. - A brief description of why you consider it suspicious. 4. **Delete** the document from your inbox and any local copies **only after** you have confirmed it is safe or after the security team advises you to do so. 5. **Stay alert**: If you receive multiple suspicious documents from the same source, inform your manager and the security team promptly. ### Why This Matters - **Malware** can be hidden in seemingly harmless files (e.g., PDFs, Office documents) and can compromise your workstation, the corporate network, and sensitive company data. - **Phishing** attempts often use documents to lure you into revealing credentials or financial information. - Prompt reporting helps the security team contain threats quickly and protect the entire organization. If you ever have doubts about a document, it’s always safer to **report first** rather than risk opening it. Feel free to reach out to the security team or HR if you need further clarification.
